services.name: OpenAI API
services.description: OpenAI's managed API platform for its text, reasoning, image, audio, realtime, embedding, moderation, and related model families.
services.service_boundary: Represents the developer API platform, not ChatGPT, Codex, individual model releases, or Azure-hosted OpenAI models.
services.regional_controls: Eligible API organizations can configure project-level regional storage and, for supported regions, regional processing; eligibility and endpoint coverage vary.
services.retention_controls: API data is not used for model training unless the customer opts in. Default abuse-monitoring and application-state retention vary by endpoint; approved organizations can use Modified Abuse Monitoring or Zero Data Retention with documented feature limitations.
services.routing: Customers select models within OpenAI's catalog; the service is not a cross-provider routing layer.
services.customization: Fine-tuning and stored application resources are available for eligible models and endpoints, with separate retention behavior.
strengths: One first-party platform spans multiple modalities, realtime interaction, tools, batch processing, and model customization.
Project-level administration, data controls, and regional endpoints are documented in the API platform.
tradeoffs: Regional processing, Zero Data Retention, and some enterprise controls require eligibility and do not cover every endpoint or feature.
The service exposes OpenAI models rather than a vendor-neutral catalog.

services.name: Anthropic API
services.description: Anthropic's managed first-party API for Claude models, including Messages, streaming, prompt caching, files, and asynchronous message batches.
services.service_boundary: Represents Anthropic's direct commercial API, not Claude.ai, Claude Code, model access through Bedrock or Vertex AI, or individual Claude releases.
services.regional_controls: Commercial API access is limited to Anthropic's supported countries and regions; the reviewed direct-API sources do not establish customer-selected processing regions.
services.retention_controls: Standard API inputs and outputs are deleted from backend systems within 30 days, subject to policy-enforcement and legal exceptions. Approved enterprise API customers may receive Zero Data Retention, with documented exceptions for features such as files and some batch or caching behavior.
services.routing: Customers select Claude models within Anthropic's direct API; access to Claude through other cloud platforms is a separate inference-service boundary.
services.customization: The reviewed API emphasizes prompt caching, files, tools, and batch execution rather than customer-deployed model weights.
strengths: The direct Messages API provides a focused first-party contract for Claude capabilities.
Anthropic publishes separate commercial retention guidance and a documented enterprise Zero Data Retention boundary.
tradeoffs: The direct service is limited to Anthropic model families.
Zero Data Retention is approval-based and feature-specific exceptions still require review.

services.name: Amazon Bedrock
services.description: AWS's managed foundation-model platform for invoking, customizing, evaluating, and governing Amazon and third-party models within AWS accounts and regions.
services.service_boundary: Represents the Amazon Bedrock inference platform, not Amazon's model families, SageMaker-hosted endpoints, Amazon Q, or Bedrock AgentCore.
services.regional_controls: Model, feature, and endpoint availability is region-specific. Inference profiles can route within a geography or globally, while single-region use and provisioned capacity have separate support matrices.
services.retention_controls: Data handling depends on the selected model, Bedrock feature, region, AWS account controls, and any applicable third-party model terms; cross-region profiles can change the processing locations involved.
services.routing: Bedrock inference profiles can route a selected model across supported AWS regions; this is regional capacity routing rather than arbitrary cross-model selection.
services.customization: Eligible base models can be customized, and imported or custom models use distinct identifiers and capacity requirements.
strengths: One AWS control plane covers models from several publishers, regional IAM boundaries, and multiple capacity modes.
Inference profiles and provisioned throughput support production capacity and residency choices.
tradeoffs: Availability and API compatibility vary by model, endpoint, feature, and AWS region.
Third-party models can add publisher-specific terms on top of the AWS agreement.

services.name: Vertex AI Generative AI
services.description: Google Cloud's managed generative-AI platform for accessing Google, partner, open, and customer-deployed models through Vertex AI and Model Garden.
services.service_boundary: Represents managed generative inference on Vertex AI, not Gemini Apps, Google AI Studio, individual Gemini releases, or the broader Vertex AI agent platform.
services.regional_controls: Availability, data residency, and processing location depend on the selected model, endpoint type, and Google Cloud region; serverless and self-deployed Model Garden paths have different boundaries.
services.retention_controls: Data governance follows the selected Vertex AI service, project configuration, model publisher, and Google Cloud terms; customers must review model- and feature-specific documentation rather than infer one platform-wide rule.
services.routing: The platform provides a common cloud control plane across model sources, but the reviewed service is not represented as an automatic latency- or price-based cross-provider router.
services.customization: Model Garden supports managed APIs, tuning, and deployment paths for eligible Google, partner, open, and customer models, including dedicated endpoints for self-deployed models.
strengths: Model Garden combines first-party, partner, open, and customer deployment paths with Google Cloud governance.
Serverless, provisioned, batch, and dedicated deployment choices cover distinct production needs.
tradeoffs: Serving mode, region support, terms, and operational responsibility differ substantially across model categories.
The broad platform boundary requires model-specific review before treating any capability as universal.

services.name: OpenRouter
services.description: A unified API and billing layer that routes model requests across multiple upstream inference providers and model publishers.
services.service_boundary: Represents OpenRouter's API routing service, not the upstream providers, the underlying model releases, or OpenRouter's end-user chat interface.
services.regional_controls: Enterprise customers can use documented EU in-region routing; provider and endpoint selection otherwise determines where upstream processing occurs.
services.retention_controls: OpenRouter documents opt-in prompt logging and per-request controls that restrict routing by upstream retention or data-collection policy; upstream provider behavior remains part of the effective boundary.
services.routing: Requests can use ordered providers, fallbacks, allowlists, denylists, privacy requirements, price ceilings, and latency or throughput preferences.
services.customization: The public service focuses on routing existing models and provider endpoints; private customer endpoints are documented separately as an enterprise beta and are not treated as a stable catalog capability here.
strengths: A single compatible API can express fallback, cost, latency, throughput, and data-policy constraints across providers.
Endpoint-level retention metadata makes privacy part of routing rather than a provider-wide assumption.
tradeoffs: Requests cross an additional service boundary before reaching an upstream inference provider.
Effective terms, availability, and data handling depend on both OpenRouter and the selected upstream endpoint.

services.name: GroqCloud
services.description: Groq's managed inference service for a selected production and preview catalog of openly available text, audio, safety, and compound AI models and systems.
services.service_boundary: Represents the GroqCloud developer API, not GroqChat, Groq Playground, Groq hardware, individual hosted models, or third-party model publishers.
services.regional_controls: Reviewed documentation states that retained customer data is stored in United States Google Cloud buckets; the pilot does not claim customer-selected inference regions.
services.retention_controls: Inference inputs and outputs are not retained by default except for reliability or abuse handling; customers can enable Zero Data Retention. Batch, fine-tuning, and other stateful features have separate retention behavior.
services.routing: Customers select among models hosted by Groq; Flex processing changes capacity behavior but is not a multi-provider routing layer.
services.customization: Fine-tuning and LoRA state are documented as retained until customer deletion; support and availability remain model-specific.
strengths: The service documents production versus preview models, token-speed signals, and OpenAI-compatible access.
On-demand, Flex, and batch paths expose distinct capacity and workload tradeoffs.
tradeoffs: The hosted catalog is selective and preview models may be discontinued on short notice.
Regional choice is narrower than multi-region cloud platforms in the reviewed documentation.
